# IBPS PO — 12-week study plan

**Assumption:** roughly **2.5–3 hours a day**, six days a week. That is about 18 hours a
week, which is enough to go from "I do not know the syllabus" to "I can clear the
sectional cut-offs" in twelve weeks.

**If you have less time**, the plan still works — cut the number of practice sets, not
the concepts. Never cut the current-affairs tracker; it is the only thing that cannot
be compressed later.

---

## The three levels

Every topic in this section is written in three layers. Use the level that matches where
you are.

| Level | What it means | Time per topic |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Concept** | You have never seen it. Learn what it is, the standard method, and one worked example | 2–3 hours |
| **2 — Speed** | You understand it. Now do it in under 60 seconds, reliably, under a timer | 3–4 hours of drills |
| **3 — Advanced** | You are fast at the standard cases. Now learn the twists, the multi-step variants and the Mains-level difficulty | 2–3 hours |

**Most candidates stop at level 1 and wonder why their score will not move.** Level 2 is
where the marks are. Level 3 is what separates a Prelims qualifier from a Mains
qualifier.

---

## The daily structure

**Do not study in one block.** Three short sessions beat one long one, because attention
decays and the material is different in kind.

| Session | Minutes | What | Why |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Morning** | 45 | **Concept work** — one new topic, read the note and the worked example | Needs a clear head |
| **Afternoon/evening** | 45 | **Speed drills** — 20–30 questions of one topic, timed | Repetition builds fluency |
| **Night** | 20 | **Current affairs tracker** — read and add 3–5 lines, then revise the last 7 days from memory | This is the habit that pays |
| **Weekend** | 3 hours | **One full mock + the 45-minute analysis** | The only thing that shows you the truth |

**Never skip the night session**, even when the mock went badly. Current affairs is the
one thing that cannot be caught up.

---

## Week by week

### Phase 1 — Foundation (weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** you have met every topic once and can do the easy questions in each section.

| Week | Quant | Reasoning | English | Also |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Percentage, ratio, proportion, average, LCM/HCF, number system | Syllogism, inequality, coding-decoding, blood relation, direction | The seven grammar rules, error spotting | Start the **current-affairs tracker** |
| **2** | Profit & loss, SI/CI, simplification, approximation, number series | Puzzles (linear), seating (linear) | Reading comprehension — 2 passages a day | Banking awareness: accounts, cards, deposits, loans |
| **3** | Time & work, time-speed-distance, mixture, ages, partnership | Puzzles (circular, floor, box), machine I/O | Cloze test, para jumbles | RBI: functions, monetary policy, MPC, inflation indices |
| **4** | DI: table, bar, line, pie | Inequality (quantity comparison) | Vocabulary, sentence improvement | Indian economy: GDP, inflation, fiscal vs monetary |

**Week 4 checkpoint:** a full Prelims mock. Expect **35–45/100**. That is fine. The
point is to see which sections are broken.

---

### Phase 2 — Speed (weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** every section is now at level 2 — you can do the standard question in under a
minute.

| Week | Focus | Daily drill |
|---:|---|---|
| **5** | **DI deep dive** — caselets, missing data, mixed sets | 1 DI set a day, 20 min. Caselet base-unit drill every day |
| **6** | **Puzzle deep dive** — 3 puzzles a day, timed, with a table | One puzzle type per day: linear, circular, floor, box, scheduling |
| **7** | **Quant arithmetic** — TSD, boats, pipes, mensuration, P&C, probability | 30 questions a day, timed at 12 min, calculator-free |
| **8** | **English speed** — RC technique, grammar drills, vocabulary | 1 RC passage a day + 15 grammar questions |

**Weeks 5–8 checkpoint:** a full Prelims mock. Expect **50–60/100**. If you are still
below 45, the problem is not speed — go back to the concept for the weakest section
and cut the mock frequency in half.

---

### Phase 3 — Mains (weeks 9–11)

**Goal:** the Mains-only content, plus the breadth that Prelims does not need.

| Week | Focus |
|---:|---|
| **9** | **Banking & Economy depth** — financial institutions, capital markets, insurance, Budget, Economic Survey, schemes, committees. Build the static GK sheet |
| **10** | **Computer aptitude** — fundamentals, OS, MS Office, networking, DBMS, digital banking. **Verify every Office shortcut yourself** |
| **11** | **Mains-level reasoning and DI** — data sufficiency, critical reasoning, statement & assumption, advanced caselets, missing-DI sets |

**Weeks 9–11 checkpoint:** a full **Mains** mock. Expect **90–120/200**. The descriptive
paper is separate — start writing one essay a week from week 9, timed at 15 minutes.

---

### Phase 4 — Consolidation (week 12)

**Goal:** not new marks. The same marks, reliably, under pressure.

| Day | What |
|---|---|
| **Mon–Thu** | Two timed section sets per day (one weak section, one strong section) |
| **Fri** | One full Prelims mock + full analysis |
| **Sat** | One full Mains mock (or a section mock) + analysis. Revise the formula sheet twice |
| **Sun** | Formula sheet from memory, the last 30 days of current affairs, and **rest** |

**Nothing new in week 12.** If you have not covered something by then, you will not
cover it in seven days — and you will have lost the confidence that comes from being
well prepared.

---

## The topic ladder

**How to use the topic notes in this section, at each level.**

| Topic | Level 1 — concept | Level 2 — speed | Level 3 — advanced |
|---|---|---|---|
| **English** | Learn the seven grammar rules; do 20 error-spotting questions a day | 2 RC passages a day, timed at 8 min each | Inference and theme questions; para jumbles with 5 sentences |
| **Quant** | Learn the method for each topic; no timer | 30 questions a day per topic, timed, no calculator | Caselet DI, missing DI, data sufficiency, quantity comparison |
| **Reasoning** | Learn the puzzle method and draw every table | 3 puzzles a day, timed, most-constrained-first | Scheduling puzzles, coded syllogism, advanced machine I/O |
| **Computer** | Read the note; verify every shortcut in the actual software | Weekly revision of the one-page facts | RBI circular reading; digital-banking new developments |
| **Banking/Economy** | Learn the static facts and build the GK sheet | Daily tracker + weekly revision | RBI circular interpretation; budget and economic-survey analysis |

---

## Mock cadence

| Week | Mocks | Notes |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1–4 | 0–1 | Learn the syllabus first. Mocks before this measure nothing useful |
| 5–8 | 1 per week | Start after the week-4 checkpoint |
| 9–11 | 2 per week | One Prelims, one Mains, alternating |
| 12 | 2–3 | Prelims only. No Mains mocks in the final week — they are longer and raise your stress |

**Always analyse the same day.** See the [PYQ analysis note](./07-previous-year-analysis.md)
for the 45-minute routine.

**One mock is worth less than one analysed mock.** If you can only do one mock a week,
do it and analyse it properly — that beats three unanalysed mocks.

---

## The three habits that decide the outcome

### 1. The current-affairs tracker, from day one

20 minutes every night. One page per month. One line per item. This is the habit that
cannot be compressed into the last month, and it is worth 15–30 marks in Mains.

### 2. Speed drills, every single day

20–30 questions of one topic, timed, without a calculator. Speed is a skill that only
drills build. A candidate who knows all the concepts but takes 90 seconds per Quant
question will not clear the sectional cut-off.

### 3. Analysing every mock

45 minutes after every mock. Tag each error, write down exactly three fixes, and track
your section-wise scores in a six-column table. After six mocks this table is a
complete diagnosis of where you stand.

---

## If you have only four weeks

**Week 1** — Quant arithmetic (percentage, ratio, average, P&L, SI/CI, simplification,
series) + the seven English grammar rules + syllogism and inequality.

**Week 2** — DI (all types, including caselets) + puzzles (linear and circular) + RC
technique + banking awareness basics.

**Week 3** — Speed: 30 timed questions a day per section, one full mock on Sunday.

**Week 4** — Two mocks a week with full analysis, formula sheet revision, current-affairs
tracker from day one.

**The four pillars, in order:** Quant/DI → Reasoning puzzles → English → Banking. That
order maximises the marks you can bank per hour of learning.

---

## If you have six months

Do the twelve weeks above, then:

1. **Repeat the Phase 2 drills** at a higher intensity — this is where the score comes
   from.
2. **Add Mains-only depth** — data sufficiency, critical reasoning, caselet DI at
   Mains difficulty, computer aptitude, banking and economy.
3. **Write two descriptive answers a week** from week one of the second phase.
4. **Sit a mock every three days** and keep the tracking table for the whole six months.
5. **Add a second current-affairs pass** — a monthly revision of the tracker from six
   months ago.
